::: {#exm-konigsberg-euler}
#### No walk over each bridge once

The people of K&ouml;nigsberg asked whether they could walk through the city, cross each bridge exactly once, and come back to where they started.
In 1736, Leonhard Euler showed that they could not [@wikipedia_seven_bridges_of_konigsberg].
In the graph of @exm-konigsberg, such a walk is an Euler circuit (@def-euler-circuit).
The graph is connected (@def-connected), since $D$ is adjacent (@def-adjacent) to $A$, $B$ and $C$.
The degrees are

$$
\deg(A) = 5, \quad \deg(B) = 3, \quad \deg(C) = 3, \quad \deg(D) = 3,
$$

all odd, so the graph has no Euler circuit, by @thm-euler-circuit.

:::
